title: Organize Your Relationships by Location and Activity
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This entry offers a simple relationship-maintenance system: organize your network by city and by shared activities or interests, so travel and event planning naturally surfaces who to reconnect with. It emphasizes that generating a master list of relationships is itself a valuable exercise in deciding who is worth continued investment. The piece stresses that the act of inviting someone communicates their importance, regardless of whether they can attend. It closes by framing this as a tedious but worthwhile system for preventing the common regret of forgetting to reach out to someone nearby.
points: The system organizes personal and professional relationships by city and by shared interests or activities.
Building the master list itself is described as a valuable exercise in prioritizing which relationships matter most.
The invitation itself, not just the visit, is what signals someone's importance to you.
The system is framed as tedious but effective at preventing missed opportunities to reconnect.
quotes: As your network of relationships expands, it becomes increasingly hard to keep track of the many people you know and value.
The best way to remedy your faulty memory is to organize your relationships by city and activity.
Purposely deciding who is worth your time and energy brings the value of your relationships into sharp relief.
It is important to remember that it is the invitation that tells people they are important to you.
Organizing relationships by location and activity sounds like common sense, but it is not a common practice.
Your memory is limited, especially when you get busy. Eliminate regrets and apologies after the fact with this simple approach.
